meta: Aqua Shard and Hutong are the efficient end: 188 schedules at about £13.80 and 209 at about £9.52, both inside the good band, and both stepped spend up week on week.

Regent St spent £1,710 for 84 schedules at about £20.36 and Azzurra £861 for 46 at about £18.72; both sit between the good and poor marks, and Regent St's spend rose 54 percent week on week for 12 extra schedules.
Shiro Sushi cut spend to £320 and took 21 schedules at about £15.25, roughly at the good threshold but on the smallest base in the portfolio.
google: Aqua Shard Google delivered about 307 booking conversions on £3,332, roughly £10.85 each, the best value in the portfolio, helped by a new Afternoon Tea search campaign.
Hutong ran £1,966 for about 187 conversions at roughly £10.51, still inside the good band, though conversions read well below last week's 327.

Regent St at about £27.86 is close to the £30 poor mark, with conversions down from 83 to 51 on flat spend. Current-week Google conversions are not fully attributed yet, so every CPA here will settle lower.
ga4: The portfolio booked 3,015 against a 3,894 target, 22.6 percent short, up 0.8 percent week on week and 9.4 percent below last year.

Aqua Shard is the whole of the year on year gap: 1,127 against 1,861. Users are down only 9 percent, so this is conversion rate (4.3% against 6.5% last year) and a much smaller paid search base, not a traffic collapse.
Regent St (-26.5% WoW), Shiro Sushi (-20.2% WoW) and Azzurra (-7.2% WoW) all gave ground, while Hutong grew 9.4 percent week on week and is 15.1 percent ahead of last year.
